source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The original status-pref landing counted disabled extensions too, because it considered later re-enabling after a channel change. The fixed checkInstalledExtensions instead counts active non-special extensions and active non-special experiments outside its allowlist. MailGlue now refreshes these prefs on enable/disable as well as install/uninstall. Manifest parsing uses allSettled and excludes failed parse results; true defaults do not by themselves prove conservative results after failures. The checked browser test covers normal extension/experiment install/uninstall transitions, not parse failures or disabled add-ons. This is scoped source behavior, not a release-channel recommendation or a runtime result.
title: Extension targeting status uses parsed active add-ons in the fixed source
